links.reason: The two verses do press a related objection: 302 asks how formless consciousness can have தீட்டு ஒட்டு கலப்பு யாப்பு with a body that has form (உருவாய உடம்பு), and 745 asks how a soul with no தீண்டலும் ஒட்டலும் with nature can cause seeing and experiencing (காண்டற்கும் துய்த்தற்கும் காரணம்). But in 302 she grants formlessness (அருவாதலால் ... பெருவாதம் அங்கில்லை), so the point is not that the formless cannot touch the formed. The teaches line also rests on a body-sized soul that neither verse names.
links.text_issue: 745 line 3 carries a repaired TSCII leftover (தேரின்).

links.reason: Both verses really have the image of flower scent passing through a new pot into water (புத்தோடு, தண்ணீர்), so this is a shared image. Neelakesi uses it against the Buddhist trace (வாசனை யாதினதாகும்), not to limit the quatrain's teaching on good company. The claims that the Naladiyar 'quietly assumes' a theory of transmission, and that the image explains why the Buddhist chose it, are not in either text.
links.text_issue: 622 line 3 (ஓதன கந்தம்) is unclear; the marker flagged the sense.

links.reason: The preface's கடவுள் பத்தினிக் கற்கோள் வேண்டி ... ஆரிய அண்ணலை வீட்டி ... கங்கை மண்ணி is the campaign for the stone, and the epic unit goes on to the temple (பத்தினிக் கோட்டம்), its daily festival (நித்தல் விழாவணி) and the boon begged by the freed Aryan kings and Gajabahu (தந்தேன் வரம்). The note and teaches report both ends accurately, and the gains are hedged honestly about how late the preface is.

The courtesan house prices the garland at the king's reward (ஆயிரத்து எண்கழஞ்சு ... பெறுவது இம் மாலை) and Kovalan forgets his home (மனையகம் மறந்து), so the couplet's mercenary women (பொருள்விழையும் ஆய்தொடியார்) are relevant. But the couplet's subject is the sweet speech of women who do not love, and the scene has neither that speech nor a Madhavi shown to lack love. The pairing is mostly a shared theme, and the claim that the couplet's warning 'must reach the custom and the buyer' is the link's own extension.
links.text_issue: Repaired line 158; the marker flagged the sense.

links.reason: Both poems have a broken oath sworn with the sea as witness (கடல்தெய்வம் காட்டிக் காட்டி அரியசூள் பொய்த்தார் / சூளும் பொய்யோ கடல்அறி கரியே). But the spoiled sand-play (வண்டற் பாவை சிதைய), which teaches and gains both credit to the vari, is not in this stanza. A sea-oath is a stock neythal motif, so 'evidence that its situation had become a fixed piece of Puhar song' is more than one stanza shows.

Neelakesi 74 promises to teach birth, the diseases born within it and the medicine of dharma that cuts them (அப்பிணியினைத் துணிக்கும் அறவியின் மருந்து). Pattinathar's medicine is against dying (இறவாதிருக்க மருந்து), and he does not call birth a disease, so 'agree on the diagnosis' overstates it. The contrast between grace and one's own dharma is real, but it rests on 74's silence in a verse that only introduces the sermon.

Both units use the same stock example of gram cooked into a mash (கும்மாயம்; Manimekalai பயற்றுத் தன்மை கெடாது கும்மாயம் இயற்றி), and the teaches point about which side voices the objection is fair. But the two make no incompatible claims: the Manimekalai reports the Jain example and Mokkalan attacks it in a debate the Jain work then answers. That is a shared example, not a tension.

One list is of false semblances of knowing (பிரமாண ஆபாசங்கள், shell for silver) and the other of false thesis, reason and example (பக்கப் போலி, ஏதுப் போலி, திட்டாந்தப் போலி). The later unit does not answer or limit the earlier one; they are parallel catalogues of error. The teaches claim that error moves away from 'mistaken seeing' is undercut by the first false thesis named, பிரத்தியக்க விருத்தம் (against perception), and by the fact that only the four அப்பிரசித்த kinds concern terms the opponent does not grant.

The only link is the word எஃகு: wealth is the sharpest steel for cutting a foe's pride (செருக்கறுக்கும்), and help to a fallen foe (ஊராண்மை) is valour's edge. The two couplets address different topics, wealth and valour, and they do not contradict each other. 'Cutting and sparing are both called sharpness' is only the shared word.

Neelakesi mocks the one who calls earth, water, city, fire and clan பொய், saying only his own deceit is not false (சலம் பொய் அன்று இது ஒன்றே நுங்கள் சத்தையே). Pambatti tells the reader to be clear that the world is false (சகத்தைப் பொய் என்று தெளிந்து). On the plain reading these are incompatible claims about whether the world is real, and the note rightly frames 534 as the Jain account of a Buddhist teacher.

Both say that evil speech does not come from the mouths of the good (ஒல்லாவே தீய வழுக்கியும் வாயாற் சொலல் / கற்றார்வாய் ... தோன்றா கரப்புச்சொல்). The teaches contrast of a slip against 'even if they die' depends entirely on emending சாயிறுந் to சாயினும். With that word in doubt, the agreement is the shared theme.
links.text_issue: Nanmanikkadigai 96 line 2 சாயிறுந் is probably corrupt.

links.reason: The close of the Silappathikaram declares its matter completed upon Manimekalai (மணிமேகலைமேல் உரைப்பொருள் முற்றிய), and the Manimekalai patikam has Saathan set out மணிமேகலை துறவு with Ilango listening (இளங்கோ வேந்தன் அருளிக் கேட்ப). The pair is a real frame-to-frame continuation, and the note's point about the reversed roles of composer and listener is accurate.
links.text_issue: Line 17 can be read as the work or the person Manimekalai; the link holds on either reading.

links.reason: Saathuvan's ban is மயக்கும் கள்ளும் மன் உயிர் கோறலும் கடிந்தனர், liquor and killing with no word on eating flesh. Neelakesi argues that those who shun toddy (கள்வரைந்தார்) must for the same reason shun flesh (புலால்வரையார்). The gap is real, but it is an argument from one line's silence in a story speech, and the Neelakesi does not address that text, so 'exploits exactly that gap' is the pairing's construction.

Both read the sneeze as a sign of the absent lover's thought (அடுத்தடுத்து ஒள்ளிய தும்மல் / தும்மல் சினைப்பது போன்று கெடும்). Different bodily outcomes lead to different verdicts, but that is the same belief applied to two situations, not incompatible claims, so the type is wrong. The teaches line itself describes it as a shared belief.
links.text_issue: The marker flagged Ainthinai Ezhupathu 41's sense.

links.reason: The unit has the courtesan who casts him off as காணம் இலி and dice (வட்டினும் சூதினும்), so the couplet's இருமனப் பெண்டிர் and கவறு fit his ruin, though liquor is not in this unit. The claim that his refusal on the island 'is what brings fortune back' is not in the text: the Naga chief's treasure comes after Saathuvan teaches him dharma, not as the result of abstaining. The 'reversal' the couplet is said to gain is the link's own moral.

Kayasandigai sends Manimekalai to Aathirai (அவள் மனை இம் மனை நீ புகல்வேண்டும்), and Aathirai fills the bowl (ஆதிரை இட்டனள் ஆருயிர்மருந்து). That is the plot carrying out an instruction, close to plain sequence. The irony that a wife whose husband left her for a courtesan feeds the courtesan's daughter is real and adds something. Manimekalai's line 73-74 calls such alms of great worth (பெருந் தகவு உடைத்து); it does not make them a rule for the first alms.

The benediction praises the moon because it is like the Chola's cool white umbrella (குளிர்வெண் குடைபோன்று இவ் அங்கண் உலகு அளித்தலான்). The venba makes the moonlit night like the guardian's white umbrella that is shade to those joined and heat to those not (கூடினார் பால் நிழலாய்க் கூடார்ப்பால் வெய்தாய்), and sets Madhavi as கூடிய against an unnamed Kannaki. The later use gives the earlier image its other edge, which the teaches line states correctly.

The two lines are identical in both units: பசியும் பிணியும் பகையும் நீங்கி வசியும் வளனும் சுரக்க. In one they are spoken by possessed old women (வலவையின் உரைக்கும் மூதிற் பெண்டிர்), in the other by the drummer proclaiming the festival (கண் முரசு இயம்பி ... அணி விழா அறைந்தனன்). The shift from a trance blessing to a civic proclamation is accurately described. The direction of borrowing is a reading, but a plausible one.

The pillar says the prince died by his own ஊழ்வினை, yet Kanchanan's வெவ் வினை will not leave him (அவ் வினை நின்னையும் அகலாது ஆங்கு உறும்), which answers to the couplet's ruin that stays at the feet (வீயாது அடி உறைந்தற்று). The epic does not limit the rule; it adds a hard case in which the rule still holds, which makes it a development, not a qualification. Apart from the type, teaches and gains are accurate.
links.text_issue: The marker flagged line 122 (கைம்மை கொள்ளேல்) as uncertain.

links.reason: Kavunthi's ஒய்யா வினைப்பயன் உண்ணுங் காலைக் கையாறு கொள்ளார் கற்றறி மாக்கள் is the couplet's calm before what comes (அன்றாங்கால் அல்லற் படுவது எவன்). She adds learning as its ground and desire for women and food as a cause of suffering (பெண்டிரும் உண்டியும் இன்பம் என்று ... கொள்ளாத் துன்பம்). The teaches line names what the epic adds.

The colophon of Patitruppattu 43 names the same king, and its war from the Himalaya to Kumari (வடதிசை எல்லை இமயமாகத் தென்னங் குமரியொடு ஆயிடை அரசர் ... ததைய) is the kind of fame the minister invokes when he says none will oppose him (ஏற்பவர் முதுநீர் உலகில் முழுவதும் இல்லை). The epic applies the poem's praise as a political argument; it does not limit it, so develops fits better than qualifies. Apart from the type, teaches and gains hold.

The couplet says a ruler endures by just rule, and without it his lustre does not last (மன்னாவாம் மன்னர்க்கு ஒளி). The Vanchi song repeats the Chera's saying that Pandyas do not live once the sceptre bends (செங்கோல் வளைய உயிர்வாழார் பாண்டியர்) and sings that as glory. The king's death for his own injustice keeps the line's ஒளி, which is a real limit on the couplet's simple equation.

In Neelakesi 116 the soul takes the threefold medicine itself (ஓர்தல் தெளிவோடு ஒழுக்கம் இவை உண்டார் ... பிறவார்). In Tirumanthiram 2075 the mind is made clear when Nandi grants grace (நந்தி அருள்தரச் சித்தம் தெளிந்தோன்). Release by one's own remedy against release by grace is an incompatible account on a defensible reading, the kind of tension this round tests, and the teaches line rightly notes that தெளிவு is a remedy in one and an effect in the other.

Kundalakesi praises her lord as one who suffered only for others (அயலார்க்கே துன்புற்றான்). Neelakesi addresses the Buddha with the same figure (கற்பமெல்லாம் பிறர்க்கே நின்று உழந்த கருணையினாய்) at the end of a verse charging him with contradiction about earth and hardness (வற்பமல்லா நிலமன்னும் தரிக்கும் என்பாய் அல்லையோ). The Buddhist's praise returned as an ironic address is a meaningful reuse.

Visakai's மிக்க அறமே விழுத் துணை ஆவது, after youth, body and wealth that do not last and sons who do not give heaven (புத்தேள் உலகம் புதல்வரும் தாரார்), matches the couplet's virtue that is பொன்றாத் துணை. Her bidding தானம் செய் to an old man also answers the couplet's அன்றறிவாம் என்னாது. The teaches line rightly sees virtue set in place of the wife and sons a householder is told he needs.

The spoiled play really recurs: a conch ploughs through the girl's sand-play (வண்டல் உழுது அழிப்ப) and a man spoils their play and goes (பொய்தல் அழித்துப் போனார்). But the 61-68 marking itself calls the spoiled sand-play a stock neythal sign, so 'Madhavi takes Kovalan's own image' claims a dependence the stanzas do not show. Line 253 says he will not leave their heart, which is softer than a charge of desertion.

The lists share only anger exactly (வெகுளி), with அவா and உலோபம் roughly alike. The Kural's envy and harsh speech are not 'from its own school', since the Kural states a general ethic and not a sect's list. Neither text limits the other, and the gain claimed for the epic side (that it strengthens her charge against the Buddhists) does not follow. It is a shared theme of fault lists dressed up as a qualification.

Both poems tell the same scene of a weeping woman before Pekan's bards: Kapilar asks யார்கொல் அளியள், and Paranar's woman answers யாம் அவன் கிளைஞரேம் அல்லேம் and names the other woman (எம்போல் ஒருத்தி நலன்நயந்து). But they are separate poems by two poets, set next to each other by the anthology. That 'each poet adds what the last withheld', with the reproach built up in turn, is a reconstructed sequence that neither poem states.

The minister's தன் உயிர்க்கு இரங்கான் பிற உயிர் ஓம்பும் shares the couplet's own terms (மன்னுயிர் ஓம்பி ... தன்னுயிர் அஞ்சும் வினை) and turns them around: the protector's mark is not to pity his own life. The couplet promises the protector safety, so the minister's use is a genuine limit, and the note does not overclaim it as a quotation.
links.text_issue: The unit opens mid-speech at line 115 (பெறுதி விரும்பினை).

links.reason: Arkkachandran's monk claims his Buddhas would not call evil conduct evil deed, since there is only mind (சித்தமே அல்லதில்லை ... தீவினை என்னல் வேண்டார்). The Buddha's own close in 493 says that those who know his four truths reach release whatever they do (எவையே செய்தும் எய்துப வீடும்). The later verse gives the earlier excuse a source in the founder's words, and teaches correctly flags that this rests on that reading and frames it as the Jain poet's move.
links.text_issue: 493 line 2 (நாட்டிலங்காட்டமிலை) is hard to divide; the marker flagged the sense.

links.reason: The shared premise is exact and real: வினையின் வந்தது வினைக்கு விளைவு ஆயது against வினைப்போகமே ஒரு தேகம். But Sudhamathi's புறமறிப்பாராய் asks a lustful prince to turn from a woman's body; she does not offer a remedy for release, so 'puts release in seeing the body truly' and the 'godless remedy' gain misdescribe her point. A contrast of remedies would also be a tension, not a qualification.

Manimekalai shows Udayakumaran an old woman's hair, brow, eyes and nose turned from their praised likenesses (வெண் மணல் ஆகிய கூந்தல், கழுநீர்க் கண் ... வழுநீர் சுமந்தன), which is the quatrain's spear-eyed woman becoming staff-eyed (வேல்கண்ணள் ... கோல்கண்ணள் ஆகும்). The epic puts the warning in the desired woman's mouth, and the prince who ignores it is killed in this same kaathai, so both gains are true.

Tirumular says there is no dharma that leaves out the Veda, and that the wise gave up argument (தர்க்க வாதத்தை விட்டு) and recited it to win release. Neelakesi argues by stacked reasons that the Veda is made (செய்கையும் புதுமையும் உடைமையின்) and, joined to killing, drives its followers to an evil birth (தீக்கதிச் செலுத்துவது). These are incompatible claims about the Veda, and the method contrast in teaches is accurate.

Maadalan's மறையோன் உற்ற வான்துயர் நீங்க உறைகவுள் வேழக் கையகம் புக்கு வானோர் வடிவம் பெற்றவன் repeats the rescue scene's கையகம் புக்கு (15:49). The verbal participle joins the deed to the god's form he won, so the earlier deed bears its fruit in the later unit. That is a real fulfilment, as the note says.

Both verses attack the Buddhist continuum (சந்தானம்): 199 says the two kinds of continuum (பின்ன, பிறிதில்) destroy what she said, and 603 asks what a feeble continuum (சவலைச் சந்தானம்) can do once the aggregates have wholly perished. These are related objections, not 'the same objection', and both verses are obscure at the point the link relies on.
links.text_issue: 199 line 4 and 603 line 2 are obscure; the marker flagged both.

links.reason: The king declares தூ அறத் துறத்தல் நன்று and credits Manimekalai. She answers that if kings take up the dharma of grace nothing else is needed (அரசர் தாமே அருளறம் பூண்டால் பொருளும் உண்டோ பிற), defines dharma as food, clothing and shelter for all, and sends him home by ship. The later unit answers and reverses the earlier one, and the teaches line is accurate.

Kannaki rejects the Kama-shrine rite for winning a husband (பீடு அன்று என இருந்த), and the venba says the gods worship her who worships her husband and no god (தெய்வந் தொழாஅள் கொழுநற் றொழுவாளைத் தெய்வந் தொழுந்தகைமை). The later verse answers the earlier refusal. The venba's first line is close enough to Kural 55's first line (தெய்வம் தொழாஅள் கொழுநன் தொழுது எழுவாள்) to support 'in the Kural's own terms'.
links.text_issue: The marker flagged 9:55 (கைத்தாயும் அல்லை) as obscure.

links.reason: The venba says they never parted (ஒருவார்), and the next kaathai has Kovalan, infatuated with Madhavi, forget his home (விடுதல் அறியா விருப்பினன் ... மனையகம் மறந்து). A claim followed by the scene that refutes it is a valid within-epic link. The irony of நிலையாமை கண்டவர்ப்போல் is a reading, but a fair one. 'Within one kaathai' is loose, since the reversal comes in the next kaathai.
links.text_issue: தூமப் பணிகள் (2:91) is uncertain in its first word.

links.reason: The narrator calls the rite புலை சூழ் வேள்வி, and the boy steals the cow to end its suffering. The brahmins catch him, beat him, call him புலைச் சிறு மகனே and say போக்கப்படுதி. The couplet weighs not killing above a thousand oblations (அவிசொரிந் தாயிரம் வேட்டலின்), and the epic counts the social cost of acting on that, which the couplet does not. 'Called a thief' is slightly loose: the Tamil charges him with taking the cow rather than using the word thief.

Both question outward marks: the couplet says neither shaving nor long hair is needed (மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும் வேண்டா), and Neelakesi asks what covering is for (மூடிற்றின் பயன் என்னை). But her argument is a dilemma between release and dignity, not an appeal to the maxim, so 'the Jain debater uses it' is not in the text. The point about her own tradition's nakedness is in neither verse.

On the marker's reading, the venba's நிலையாமை கண்டவர்ப்போல் makes impermanence a reason to enjoy the pleasures of marriage, and the quatrain mocks one who marries after seeing a corpse carried out (மணம் கொண்டு ஈண்டு உண்டுண்டுண்டு என்னும்). That conflict depends on one reading of an ambiguous simile, and the note does not say so. The other-side gain is false: the lovers do not 'claim to have seen it', since the narrator says only 'as if' (கண்டவர்ப்போல்).

links.reason: 203's sixth thing is a power (சத்தி) said to pass across the moments, and 480's is a person joined by reasoning (புற்கலன் உளன் எனப் புணர்ப்பு). Neither verse says the person stands beside the five aggregates, and 480's charge is a list of contradictions that does not refer back to 203's dilemma. Equating the power with the person is what makes the link work.
links.text_issue: 480 line 3 differs from 478 line 3 (போதியால் / புந்தியால்); one reading is likely a copyist's slip.
